Combine videos

Combine Videos into One MP4

Choose two or more video clips, put them in playback order, then download one MP4. The first clip sets the output shape. Other clips fit inside it, and each clip’s sound plays in its own segment. The browser processes your files locally.

Merge your video clips

Up to 250 MiB and 2 minutes in total.
    Download merged MP4

    To try it, download the four-second landscape clip with sound and the six-second silent portrait clip. Choose both files together.

    1. Combine two or more clips
    2. Choose the playback order and shape
    3. Check the video at the join
    4. Input and output formats

    Set the order and the output shape

    Use Up and Down to arrange the clips in the order they should play. Put a portrait clip first if you want a portrait result. The output uses the first clip’s aspect ratio, with the longest side capped at 1,280 pixels. Other clips are fitted inside the canvas and can have black bars.

    To shorten a clip first, trim it by start and end time. If you prefer different framing on a clip, crop the visible area before merging.

    Play across each join before sharing

    1. Check that the exported duration is close to the combined source durations. Frame and audio timing may cause small differences.
    2. Play the preview across each transition. Verify the order, framing and sound. A clip without audio stays silent for its segment.
    3. Save the MP4 and open it in the destination app before relying on it.

    A Chromium test combined a six-second silent portrait clip with a four-second landscape clip with sound. Both orders exported in about 10.03 seconds, and the sound played during the landscape segment in each result. See the test measurements.

    To make the entire result silent, remove its audio track after merging.

    Formats and local processing

    Each clip needs one video track and can have one audio track. MP4, MOV, WebM and MKV are supported when their codecs can be decoded in your browser. The combined MP4 is re-encoded as H.264 video. If any clip has sound, the output includes stereo AAC. Audio outside a clip’s video time is trimmed.

    The files stay on your device. For formats the browser cannot decode, very long material or projects with multiple audio tracks, use an editor that supports those source files. Decoding and writing use Mediabunny.
